title: Marta or Miriam daughter of Baitus
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Marta (or Miriam) daughter of Baitus was also very wealthy. She was present during the siege of Jerusalem before the destruction. [Gittin 56a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.56a.11-14) relates that Marta daughter of Baitus, a wealthy Jerusalem woman, sent her servant to buy bread during the siege, but he found none. She went out herself to find food, and animal dung stuck to her foot. According to another account, she found Rabbi Tzadok’s dried figs and became sickened. Before she died she took all her silver and gold and threw it outside, then died. Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai applied to her the verse “[The tender and delicate woman among you](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.28.56).” Hyman says that [Eichah Rabbah 1:47](https://www.sefaria.org/Eikhah_Rabbah.1.47) recounts the story with many corruptions; see there.

notes.text: The linked Bavli names Marta bat Baitus. It describes the failed purchases during the siege, then gives two accounts of her death, one involving dung and the other a single dried fig of Rabbi Tzadok. Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai applies the verse to her.

The linked Eichah Rabbah names Miriam bat Baitus and has Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok apply the same verse to her in a different account. In [Yoma 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.18a.10), the woman who secures Yehoshua ben Gamla’s appointment is called Marta. [Heilprin’s entry on Yehoshua ben Gamla](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1761&lang=en) records both name forms. Hyman characterizes the differences in Eichah Rabbah as textual corruptions.
